rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance – just cause for eviction and no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement: A San Diego landlord may end a covered tenancy only for a listed at-fault cause (such as nonpayment, an uncured lease breach after written notice, nuisance or criminal activity) or a listed no-fault cause (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, a government order, demolition or substantial remodel), and the notice must state the cause. For a no-fault termination, the landlord must pay relocation assistance of 2 months' actual rent (3 months for tenants 62+ or disabled), either directly within 15 days of the notice or as waived rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation of 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants); owner move-in requires 12 months' occupancy within 90 days; 5-year right of first refusal after no-fault eviction
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including rented dwellings in mobilehome parks, where the tenant has lawfully occupied for more than 30 days (fixed-term leases of 3 months or less are not covered). Housing whose certificate of occupancy was issued within the previous 15 years is exempt (except mobilehomes). Relocation is owed regardless of tenant income or length of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels and occupancies of 30 days or less; housing restricted as affordable by deed, regulatory or subsidy agreement (Section 8 voucher tenants remain covered); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospital, religious, care and transitional housing; school dormitories; tenant shares a bath or kitchen with a resident owner; owner-occupied single-family home renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex (neither unit an ADU or JADU); separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, if the tenant got written notice of the exemption; certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years. No relocation is owed if a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for the condition behind a vacate order.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§ 98.0701 et seq.)
rules.penalty: Wrongful eviction liability of at least 3x actual economic damages; failure to pay relocation makes the landlord liable for at least 3x the required relocation plus actual economic damages; injunctive relief, punitive damages and discretionary attorney's fees (outside unlawful detainer); noncompliant termination notices are void; violation is an affirmative defense in unlawful detainer; City civil and criminal enforcement.

exemption_tests.description: Certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes)
Owner-occupied duplex where the owner lives in one unit as principal residence since the start of the tenancy (neither unit an ADU or JADU)
Owner-occupied single-family home where the owner rents no more than 2 units or bedrooms

rules.reason: All four candidates describe provisions (just cause grounds and § 98.0706(c) relocation assistance) of the same San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance, so they merge into one record citing the official municipal code text.
